A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we demonstrated the high capacity of LiNiO2 by suppressing the formation of a secondary phase and by stabilizing the structure via a rock salt phase.

a high capacity Li[Ni1-x-yCoxMnyO2] (x = 0.1-0.95, y = 0.05-0.025) can be synthesized with a high reversible capacity and excellent cycling stability, and the high reversible capacity is attributed to the formation of a rock salt structure in the deliathiated state which would otherwise be inactive for electrochemical reaction.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the rock salt phases can be beneficial for the electrochemical performance of the Ni rich cathode materials.

the excess Li ions can be used as an effective strategy to stabilize the rock salt phase, thus, to enhance the electrochemical properties of the Ni-rich Li[Ni1 yCoxMn1 yCox]O2 cathode materials for next generation Li ion batteries.
